observations: Photos 0 to 2: one horizontal foot-mounted gear reducer with a ribbed cast housing, the shape of a cycloidal (cyclo) drive.
A round motor flange with bolt holes on the input end, a solid keyed output shaft painted yellow on the other end.
Lifting eye on top plus two plugs, likely oil fill and breather.
The whole unit, bolts included, is freshly repainted blue; no nameplate, brand, ratio or rating is visible in any photo.
No motor is attached and nothing shows it turning; sits on a tiled workshop floor.
Watermark 'Ifabros Industrial, Posted on Jiji' suggests a dealer listing.

identity.kind: cycloidal gear reducer, foot mounted with motor flange
read_from: photo 0 housing shape and output shaft

claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show a foot-mounted reducer housing with input flange and output shaft.
Ribbed cast housing and feet visible in photos 0 to 2.
No nameplate or rating plate shown; the unit is repainted.

risks.risk: Rating and reduction ratio unknown; the unit may be smaller than the 15 to 20 hp claimed or have a ratio that does not suit the buyer.
risks.proof: Close photo of the nameplate, or of the flange and shaft with a tape measure across the diameters.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest size consistent with the photos, ratio unknown

risks.risk: Worn or broken internal pins, discs or bearings, hidden by the fresh paint.
risks.proof: Clip of the input turned by hand or by motor showing the output shaft turning smoothly with no knock.

risks.risk: Fresh paint over the whole unit may hide cracks, rust or welded repairs in the casting.
risks.proof: Close photos of the feet, flange and housing joints in good light.
Photo of the shaft seals after the clip, with oil in and the unit run.

proof_requests: Close photo of the nameplate or rating plate
Clip of the reducer turning, input and output both visible
Photos of the flange and shaft against a tape measure
Close photos of feet, flange and seals
response.reason: The item is plainly a cast cycloidal gear reducer, so it can be priced by type at its worst case: rating and ratio unknown and treated as not working. A nameplate and a turning clip would raise it.
